lark_e03_entry.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry.text: On the twenty-fourth morning, the pass market opened under a thin frost that disappeared wherever sunlight touched stone. Her five night room extension, paid ten copper on Day Twenty Three, included meals through Day Twenty Seven. She reached the association before the employment meeting and found Qin waiting beside a basket rack. He had come on his own repair and work route, carrying his actual papers. They greeted each other with the ease or caution their previous conversation had earned. Neither pretended they had arrived as a team. The board would receive each person's account under a different item.

lark_e03_entry_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_002.text: Inside, a charcoal brazier warmed the public room without heating every corner equally. Three voting representatives sat at the long table: one elected by freight workers, one appointed by the association's supplier members, and one representing the market households using its local passage. Lin had no vote. Her application gave her a place to answer questions about her own work, not decide the entire pass's employment or fuel. Chen sat beside the supplier representative with the comparison he had actually been hired to prepare.

lark_e03_entry_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_003.text: The supplier representative introduced himself as Rao Ji. He wore a plain dark coat with a narrow repaired seam across one elbow, and he leaned his cane against the wall only after inspecting the seat. His public work record identified six primary pairs on recovered assessments, but he did not offer Lin his current reserve or invite her to guess what he could do from the label. He asked whether her fifth-stage certificate had traveled in her own custody. She showed the permitted copy and the present clinic note together.

lark_e03_entry_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_004.text: Rao read the shoulder exclusion first. He crossed the proposed overhead guide duty out without arguing that a cultivator should find it easy. Lin felt grateful until he said the change left one less station the association could cover with its new place. He did not accuse her of causing the shortage. He asked the members whether the remaining ordinary work justified the proposed appropriation. She sat with the discomfort of being a person whose useful limits could still disappoint an employer.

lark_e03_entry_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_005.text: The worker representative wanted the new place because route notes, comparison copying and dispatch correction were currently being added to people's paid carrying work without accepted extra hours. The household representative wanted current notices that a reader could use without climbing to a private office. Rao wanted fewer disputed late deliveries and a trained worker who would stay through the term. Each could describe a practical benefit. Lin listened for the point where those benefits would require her to perform three six-hour shifts on the same day.

lark_e03_entry_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_006.text: Chen read his completed comparison of the proposed role and its exclusions. He had not decided Lin's appointment, certified the gallery or promised Duan Zhi's availability. He recommended one primary ordinary assignment, with any later alternate task accepted by its actual keeper inside the same paid shift. A field observer could not be silently turned into a loaded guide; a desk reader could not be silently made the repair contractor's unpaid advocate. Rao asked whether all those restrictions would make the new place difficult to schedule. Chen said clear restrictions would reveal the difficulty rather than create it.

lark_e03_entry_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_007.text: The association members approved a new six-hundred-copper allocation for one twenty-four-week work-and-instruction place, from the current freight season's accepted membership contributions. No archive purse, old public post appropriation or earlier commission funded it. Its paid term would run from campaign Day Twenty-eight through Day One Hundred Ninety-five. Lin had a separate ordinary account for the nights before it began and the departure days afterward. A name on the new roll would not retrospectively turn yesterday's clinic or applicant observation into association-paid work.

lark_e03_entry_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_008.text: The first category held one hundred eighty copper for forty-five accepted six-hour ordinary work shifts at four copper each. Payment would follow each completed shift's receiving. A canceled task did not earn completed-work wages; its stated cancellation or reduced-duty terms would govern separately. Qualified instruction, tests and recovery were not disguised as unpaid extra freight shifts. Lin asked whether a supervisor could extend a shift after its listed end because a load was late. The answer required a separately accepted additional task, not an interpretation of her gratitude.

lark_e03_entry_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_009.text: One hundred twenty copper bought the stated twenty-four weeks of ordinary meals and lodging at five per week. Its provider named the room, meal scope and receiving dates. It bought neither luxury nor a traveling allowance for someone else's family. The instruction and calibration category held one hundred sixty: eighty for Duan Zhi's agreed teaching scope, thirty-two for a separately appointed independent examination visit, twenty-four for independent external measurement, and twenty-four for purchased practice fuel. The examiner's final acceptance was still required; money held for a person was not that person's promise.

lark_e03_entry_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_010.text: Eighty copper reserved ordinary care and safe reduced-duty arrangements: forty for up to eight stated five-copper assessment visits, twenty for accepted ordinary treatment materials, and twenty for qualified work cover when the care terms required it. The category did not buy magical healing or guarantee Lin would qualify for the next stage. Sixty copper covered the proposed evacuation work: thirty-two for timber, sixteen for qualified crew time, eight for canvas and four for notices. Its keepers would record actual use and return unused amounts.

lark_e03_entry_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_011.text: The practice fuel purchase would receive its own measured charge record. Paying twenty-four copper would not prove any number of usable personal units, and the new appropriation did not buy the operational bell's separately owned reserve. Lin asked who could use money left in one category. The board required a new accepted amendment before transfer, with existing promises protected. She would rather have seen a larger care reserve. She said so. Rao said increasing it would require more membership money or a specific reduction elsewhere, and nobody had approved either.

lark_e03_entry_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_012.text: The independent examiner named in the proposal was Su Yan, the ninth-stage furnace examiner who had assessed Lin's earlier work. Her prospective local six-pair examination authority would be documented separately before the new tests. The proposed visit covered Days One Hundred Fifty through One Hundred Seventy-one, with its thirty-two-copper fee including the travel and room scope actually offered. She had not taught this new curriculum. She would come only after accepting the term and completing her own furnace obligations; Lin could not summon her from another town by needing an independent signature.

lark_e03_entry_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_013.text: Duan Zhi's paid instruction would preserve his current knee and cane restrictions. His recovered competence included six primary pairs, while swelling could reduce which ones he used on a given day. A comfortable demonstration from him would not prove Lin's new route. Jiang Tao retained the separate qualified apparatus role and his own local inspection conditions. Rao said the association wanted results, not a procession of respected names. Chen agreed and asked the clerk to keep the required witnessed work beside each proposed person's actual scope.

lark_e03_entry_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_014.text: The worker representative asked what happened if Lin failed an examination. The instruction category paid accepted teaching and measurement actually performed; it did not pay for a stage awarded regardless of the result. Her ordinary employment could continue inside safe accepted duties if the parties agreed and its current limits allowed it. The room did not become a debt she owed for disappointing a teacher. Lin had been ready to defend her ability to succeed. She found herself more interested in the written arrangement for surviving an honest failure.

lark_e03_entry_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_015.text: Rao asked whether she would remain through the term if another sect offered faster advancement. Lin wanted to answer with a brave promise before hearing the rest of the question. She asked for the actual exit clause instead. It allowed departure after proper notice and receiving of current duties, with unused future wages and unperformed service payments retained by their sources. No private family emergency had to be explained to the entire committee. No abrupt disappearance could leave entrusted tools without a receiver. She could accept a finite commitment without pledging every future day.

lark_e03_entry_016.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_016.text: The committee offered three primary ordinary assignments inside that approved place. A comparison-copying worker would prepare consented local examples and notices beside the lesson keeper. A route-recording worker would walk cleared ordinary passages with their actual keeper and carry no freight load by that title. A dispatch-comparison worker would help distinguish bookings, departures and deliveries with the wage reader, retaining no general authority over household packets. Their shifts paid the same stated rate. The people and questions she would meet, and the time available for other observations, would differ.

lark_e03_entry_017.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_017.text: Lin asked whether her original applicant task required her to choose the same role. The board said its received observation supplied one piece of evidence, while today's accepted assignment would need its own keeper's preparation and current clearance. She could choose a different offered role without claiming she had already performed it. Its first shift would include the ordinary local introduction and stop if the keeper found the task outside her scope. She looked toward the gallery rather than immediately selecting the work that sounded most like further cultivation.

lark_e03_entry_018.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_018.text: The market households' representative told a story about a public notice that had correctly named the closure date and left out which stair people could still use. Her father had walked uphill twice before giving up his attempt to collect a parcel. The worker representative described carrying a basket while being asked to remember a changed signal sequence nobody had written clearly. Rao described a client paying for a delivery whose tag recorded only departure. Each story wanted a different worker. Lin could hear their claims without becoming three people.

lark_e03_entry_019.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_019.text: Qin remained near the basket rack while his contractor item waited. He had not joined the employment vote or made himself the applicant's supporter. When Lin glanced toward him, he lifted the papers he had actually come to deliver and then looked back at the receiving clerk. The gesture made her smile. Ordinary people at Lark had their own work to complete while she chose a place among them. She wanted an assignment that would let her meet them repeatedly enough to learn when they preferred her help and when they wanted her to move aside.

lark_e03_entry_020.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_entry_020.text: The appointment required one primary role for its first six-week scheduling block. Later changes would need accepted new schedules and would keep the total paid shifts within the approved category. The work would put people and places into her days; her next route still required witnessed practice. Lin read the three descriptions with their actual people and receiving places. She would be paid for work finished, fed under the named lodging term, and given a bounded chance to learn. Which part of the pass would become familiar first remained hers to decide.

lark_e03_duty_choice.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_choice.text: Lin accepted the offered twenty-four-week place and selected one primary ordinary role for its initial six-week schedule. The approved wages, meals, instruction and care stayed finite; no selection paid a shift or opened a new pair. Each role would bring different people, permitted sources and observations into her working days. The other two duties remained with their current keepers rather than becoming work she could finish in her spare time.

choices.text: Take comparison copying with the lesson keeper; meet the pass through its offered examples.
Take cleared ordinary route recording; meet the carriers and their actual passages.
Take dispatch comparison; meet the workers through accepted scope and actual payment.

lark_e03_duty_copy.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_copy.text: Lin selected comparison copying. The lesson keeper, Shan Fang, received the accepted role without pretending she had gained a worker for every room. Her first shift would begin on Day Twenty-eight beside the lower school shelf. It included offered examples, public notices and readable source headings. Freight tags, private family pages and the structural keeper's repair judgments stayed elsewhere. Shan handed her a list of materials their actual authors had permitted, then asked which one Lin thought she understood too quickly.

lark_e03_duty_copy_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_copy_002.text: On the first paid morning, a worker brought two ordinary binding samples with a signed offer to describe how they behaved under his inspected basket load. One sample had been tied loosely for a rest interval, the other tightened for movement. Lin drew their apparent shapes before seeing the binder work. Shan asked her to put the timing beside the pictures. A knot could be described accurately at one moment and still mislead someone who used the drawing at another.

lark_e03_duty_copy_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_copy_003.text: The binder wanted his account to explain why a new trainee kept copying the loose resting shape. Lin listened to him demonstrate with an empty supported basket. He said the trainee was careless. Shan asked what instruction had been offered before the first error. The binder stopped and found his own draft, which had shown the same loose shape without a movement heading. Lin felt relief at the neat answer, then noticed he looked ashamed rather than delighted. She asked whether he wanted the corrected comparison offered to the trainee privately before it became a public example.

lark_e03_duty_copy_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_copy_004.text: He chose the private first reading. Lin wrote the offered explanation in the trainee's ordinary words where possible, while Shan retained the actual safety judgment with the basket keeper. They did not publish a named mistake without permission. The trainee arrived after a collecting duty and understood the two headings more readily than Lin expected. She asked why the smaller knot drawing appeared first. The binder said he had been proud of drawing it neatly. Their laughter made the room warmer without making the earlier instruction harmless.

lark_e03_duty_copy_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_copy_005.text: The afternoon brought a public notice whose large closure heading had swallowed the date beneath it. Lin copied the date at readable size and asked the keeper to verify the remaining open approach before including it. She did not invent a usable stair to make the notice kinder. The household reader who checked the copy pointed to the final line and said she could now decide whether to send her daughter for the parcel. That was the first result Lin could plainly see without writing an explanation of its importance.

lark_e03_duty_copy_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_copy_006.text: Shan received the completed first shift at its ending bell. The source copies stayed in their permitted collection; Lin retained only her own accepted comparison notes. Her work had used no powered input and granted no additional primary pair. It had introduced her to authors and readers who did not want the same thing from one page. The first four-copper wage was due only after this receiving. Tomorrow's paid work would start with an ordinary list of examples still waiting, rather than the assumption that the new worker could now explain the entire pass.

lark_e03_duty_copy_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_copy_007.text: Qin passed the open doorway carrying a basket whose actual repair state belonged to his separate receiving. He saw Lin beside the source headings and asked whether the copying room could make a replacement diagram for a torn binding notice. Shan asked him to bring its authorized source at an accepted interval. Lin could see how often useful work would arrive as an almost casual request. She had chosen a desk where those requests could become real tasks under a keeper, and where refusing to invent the missing source might make a familiar person's day harder.

lark_e03_duty_route.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_route.text: Lin selected ordinary route recording. The gallery keeper received her accepted six-week primary schedule and set the first shift for Day Twenty-eight. Its scope excluded freight carrying, overhead catching and structural certification. She would walk cleared passages, record dated observations and compare them with the people's offered use. The keeper asked whether she preferred a tidy map or a notebook with mud at the corners. Lin said she hoped to make the second useful enough that somebody could later draw the first.

lark_e03_duty_route_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_route_002.text: Her first paid morning began with a light rain that made the steps look darker without automatically closing them. The keeper performed his ordinary check before inviting her onto the posted route. Lin carried only her small notebook and stayed outside moving loads. A porter asked why an observer required permission to walk a place he used every day. The keeper said his clearance was for his accepted ordinary duty, while hers was for a different person and task. The porter considered that explanation while scraping mud off his boot.

lark_e03_duty_route_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_route_003.text: At the second landing, a mother carrying vegetables waited until three baskets had passed. The route notice described one waiting space and did not say how often it became occupied by empty packing frames. Lin asked whether she could record the woman's offered observation without her household address. She agreed and pointed to a dry corner where her child usually stood. The keeper had authority to clear the marked waiting space within the normal stacking procedure. He called the actual frame worker instead of asking Lin to move a load her title did not qualify.

lark_e03_duty_route_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_route_004.text: The frame worker disliked the request because his current storage instruction used that corner. The keeper checked both written scopes before directing the accepted change. A different designated rest space existed one turn higher, but its path had been left out of the stacking copy. Lin walked that cleared path with the worker before recording the changed location. The new note would make his ordinary task longer. She kept the added distance beside the improved waiting place instead of reporting a convenient change with no person bearing its cost.

lark_e03_duty_route_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_route_005.text: Later the keeper asked her to compare the signal view from the carrying position rather than the visitor's railing. A qualified carrier held an empty basket at its actual instructed height. Lin saw the rope signal vanish behind the basket rim. They recorded the condition and referred its work adjustment to the signal supervisor. The carrier said he had complained last month. Lin asked where his earlier offered words could be found. He named a receiver she could request, not a story she could now certify because the demonstration made it sound likely.

lark_e03_duty_route_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_route_006.text: The shift ended at its agreed bell with a received route note and unresolved signal-view question. Lin had not strengthened timber, moved freight or powered a relay. Her new four-copper wage followed the actual ordinary work. The keeper scheduled the next accepted walk and warned that weather could change its clearance before then. Lin put that condition into her calendar. She had chosen a job in which familiar steps would keep presenting new conditions, and in which the people moving across them could reasonably grow tired of being observed.

lark_e03_duty_route_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_route_007.text: Qin passed the receiving point on his own route and asked whether the upper stacking turn would now add distance to his collecting duty. The keeper checked his actual task before answering. Lin showed Qin the new dated note without claiming its useful waiting space had imposed no cost. He read the added turn and said he hoped the household reader would use it. She could not promise that response. She had chosen to meet the pass through its actual passages, including the people who would feel each sensible alteration beneath their ordinary feet.

lark_e03_duty_dispatch.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_dispatch.text: Lin selected dispatch comparison. The wage reader received her first six-week primary schedule, beginning on Day Twenty-eight. Its ordinary task concerned offered booking, departure and delivery sources, with privacy limits and payment judgments retained by the actual keeper. He asked whether she could tolerate people disliking the correct answer about a small amount. Lin said she had already disliked several correct answers about her own appointment. He laughed and gave her an unmarked receiving cover to bring to the first paid shift.

lark_e03_duty_dispatch_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_dispatch_002.text: The first shift opened with a merchant whose crate had reached the market but not its final shop. The departure tag showed completed movement to the upper receiving store. He insisted the supplier had promised the shop door. Lin asked the wage reader which actual accepted term governed that distinction. The offered booking did name the upper store; a later private conversation remained unrecorded. The merchant wanted a cheaper argument than asking its actual participants. Lin could compare the held sources without deciding what an unoffered conversation must have contained.

lark_e03_duty_dispatch_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_dispatch_003.text: A carrier came next with a damaged binding and an accurately received waiting payment. He wanted the new terms to protect the next lost collection, not merely make the old amount look correct. Lin wrote his offered proposed-terms question beneath the completed scope instead of correcting an entry that did not need correction. The reader would send that question to its accepted comparison meeting. The carrier asked whether he could bring a fellow worker. Lin checked the invitation's actual scope and gave him its stated request contact rather than an invented guaranteed place.

lark_e03_duty_dispatch_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_dispatch_004.text: At midday, an apprentice discovered he had entered a departure under the delivery column. The wage reader kept the old marks visible while correcting the scope from its actual receiving. Lin expected a lecture. Instead the reader asked which crowded line the apprentice had been following when he moved his finger. The rows had been ruled too closely for the clipboard's ordinary working position. They tried a larger interval on a permitted trial copy and found the error easier to detect. The old correction still mattered, even where its cause made blame less satisfying.

lark_e03_duty_dispatch_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_dispatch_005.text: An older household reader asked Lin to read a private return note. That task lay outside the present employment source permission. Lin directed her to the actual public receiving reader and waited until the woman knew its ordinary hours. She did not call the referral equivalent to answering now. The woman would make another walk. Lin had chosen a place where useful boundaries could be experienced as a closed door by someone arriving with a reasonable request. She wanted to learn how to explain them without pretending the additional journey was trivial.

lark_e03_duty_dispatch_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_dispatch_006.text: The wage reader received her first completed six-hour shift at the ending bell. Four copper became due for the accepted work, not for winning any dispute or making every reader content. Offered tags stayed with their actual keeper. Lin retained the permitted comparison note and the apprentice's accepted spacing question. She had used no powered input and earned no primary route from ordinary reading. The next shift would require her to hear new terms before recognizing an old form, which sounded easy only until the queue began moving.

lark_e03_duty_dispatch_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_duty_dispatch_007.text: Qin came to the window under his own basket request and collecting duty. Lin could see his repaired or still-limited equipment without turning its state into a new payment she had authority to grant. The wage reader received his actual offered scope. Qin asked whether the new work place would now make every source question quicker. Lin said it gave one bounded worker time to compare accepted records. His expression made her wish the answer had contained more immediate comfort. She had chosen a job whose limits people would hear while holding the bill for their next meal.

lark_e03_after_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_001.text: At the public receiving desk, the clerk checked the actual first-shift account against Lin's accepted assignment. He paid four copper from the work category and recorded one of the forty-five authorized shifts as completed. One hundred seventy-six remained available for future accepted work. Nobody paid the remaining term because she had signed it. Lin received the ordinary coins and remembered an earlier moment when a promised place had felt almost indistinguishable from the life it might support. This place had begun with six hours actually finished.

lark_e03_after_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_002.text: The lodging provider received the first five-copper week under the meal-and-room category, leaving the other twenty-three weeks to their own dates. Lin moved from her personally paid short-stay room into the named ordinary term room. The new room faced the quieter uphill lane and contained a shared table too small for every paper she owned. She could make it useful without treating an improved lodging as evidence of a stage she had not earned. The first thing she unpacked was her mother's letter, not the examination proposal.

lark_e03_after_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_003.text: Qin helped carry the lodging keeper's ordinary stool under his existing household arrangement, after the keeper asked him during an accepted interval. Lin moved her own light bag inside her cleared range and left the heavier work with its actual people. Qin said the room's view was less impressive than the guest room's. Lin said it might keep her from being late for supper. He wanted to know whether the promised meals would be worth their weekly price. She told him the provider had accepted a defined ordinary menu, not a duty to please every newcomer.

lark_e03_after_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_004.text: He took her to the public cooking court, where a pot of beans had been left cooling while two workers argued over a missing ladle. The ladle hung above the brazier behind a folded apron. Qin found it, held it up without speaking, and enjoyed his victory so openly that Lin laughed. The cook told him to enjoy a bowl next and stop congratulating himself while food went cold. Lin liked seeing a person who argued about damaged equipment become a person whose most urgent triumph involved soup.

lark_e03_after_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_005.text: Shan Fang came through the court carrying a repaired glove. Lin recognized the woman from her first night's supper only when she set the glove down and pulled a stubborn thread with her teeth. Qin thanked her and tried it on before asking whether she had altered the seam. She said the old seam had altered itself enough for both of them. He raised his hand to show Lin the comfortable fit. His household contained a lesson keeper who still had to cook, mend and argue, rather than a convenient supporting figure whose evenings waited for her husband's next problem.

lark_e03_after_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_006.text: Their daughter sat beneath the bench drawing a basket larger than every person around it. She asked Lin whether a cultivator could carry the drawing. Lin said she could carry that ordinary sheet if its owner wanted her to. The girl held it away and said she had meant the basket. Qin told her to ask for the basket's actual size before volunteering a stranger. Shan said he had just converted supper into the employment committee. They argued cheerfully until the child drew the basket smaller enough to fit her own favorite story.

lark_e03_after_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_007.text: Lin asked Shan whether the family's market lessons were her whole job. Shan said her ordinary accepted lesson hours belonged to the school keeper, while the household mending belonged to her own evening. Neither was another person's unlimited spare time. Then she asked whether Lin had brought any story with an ending other than a careful question. Lin thought of the mule and the dried pears. The child's attention sharpened when she reached the entangled rope. Qin insisted the mule deserved more credit than every adult who had blamed its character.

lark_e03_after_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_008.text: They finished the story without deciding that it proved a lesson about freight. Shan sent her daughter to return the bowl she had borrowed from a neighbor. The girl complained that the neighbor always wanted the same bowl back. Lin watched her leave with the ordinary object held in both hands and understood the complaint more sympathetically than she expected. Being told something belonged to someone else could be tiresome even when it was entirely true. The child came back having acquired two chestnuts and a demand to wash her hands.

lark_e03_after_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_009.text: After supper, Lin walked the public uphill lane to the small shrine used by the freight households. Its brass bell was sounded by an ordinary wooden clapper; it was not the relay's alarm. Offerings included a pear, a worn work ribbon and a folded letter addressed to someone who would not receive another delivery. Lin left the shrine's private pages unread. She stood long enough to hear the wind change around the stone corner, then asked the keeper whether visitors could place a simple grain offering without claiming the names on the household list.

lark_e03_after_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_010.text: The keeper accepted a small offered spoonful from the public bowl's stated use. Lin thought about the workers who had carried her roads before she reached the pass and about her mother's kitchen stool. She did not call the offering repayment for every cost they bore. It was one ordinary gesture she wanted to make, and the keeper could receive it without supplying a grand explanation. Below the shrine, the market lamps lit at different moments as people finished their own evening work.

lark_e03_after_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_011.text: On the way back she met Rao Ji testing an ordinary basket clasp beside a closed shop. He had no audience except the shopkeeper whose accepted repair he was checking. When he saw Lin, he asked whether her first paid shift had ended at the agreed bell. She said it had. He said the association would expect the same care from future tasks whose difficulties were less attractive than an applicant's first lesson. It sounded severe until the shopkeeper told him he had been worrying over that clasp for three days.

lark_e03_after_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_012.text: Rao lifted his hand from the clasp and admitted the shopkeeper had rejected his first repair. The latch had closed under a light test and slipped under its actual ordinary load. Lin asked whether the current comparison had solved it. He said the second repaired part had passed the keeper's stated check, while the broader problem of maintaining every clasp remained work for another day. She saw a man who had argued for useful results needing someone else to tell him he had not yet supplied one.

lark_e03_after_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_013.text: He offered to show her a stopped small-talisman task at a later accepted observation if his knee and current reserve allowed it. It would not be instruction she had secretly bought through the ordinary work place. Lin thanked him and asked for the written date when the actual keeper agreed. Rao looked amused, then said Duan would probably like that question. She felt a dangerous warmth at the hint of belonging. She could welcome it without calling the examiner's later answer already favorable.

lark_e03_after_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_014.text: Back at her room, the first wage lay beside her personal remaining coins. Four copper had come from six hours of completed work. Her room and meals now had their accepted weekly receiving; her old personal nights remained paid from her own account. She wrote the separation once and stopped adding explanations. The coins could not tell her whether the binder, carrier or household reader would trust her next question. That part of earning a place would arrive in conversations that could go badly even when the arithmetic was correct.

lark_e03_after_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_015.text: She wrote her mother about the shrine bell and the girl who wanted a drawing to become a basket. She also wrote that the new employer had accepted her current shoulder limits and offered a finite instruction place with no guaranteed stage. The sentence sounded drier than the relief behind it. Lin added that she had eaten beans and laughed at a missing ladle. Her mother might prefer that part, which was a useful correction to Lin's habit of imagining the most impressive news was always the most welcome.

lark_e03_after_016.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_016.text: A note from Jiang Tao arrived through the association's ordinary receiving. The initial apparatus inspection would take place after the keeper's accepted shutdown, with Lin invited only to observe from the cleared position. It included no novice powered input. She could attend outside her listed labor hours if she wanted, and declining would not change her already completed shift wage. Lin accepted the short observation after checking her next day's rest and work schedule. She would have another person's permission to watch a particular machine, not a claim to every demonstration the qualified surveyor could perform.

lark_e03_after_017.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_017.text: The same cover contained Duan Zhi's accepted teaching terms. His instruction would begin after the dated arrival and local recovery check, and his knee could require a supported or reduced demonstration. The paid scope bought guidance and comparisons rather than six routes delivered on demand. Lin had not yet practiced a fifth or sixth internal pair here. She put the letter beside the room's small table and felt the coming months grow less abstract. A qualified person was preparing to spend actual days answering questions she had not yet learned how to ask.

lark_e03_after_018.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_018.text: The independent examination invitation to Su Yan remained pending. The clerk's public note showed the held thirty-two-copper category and its specific prospective dates. If her acceptance did not arrive, the association would need a new properly qualified arrangement before presenting any candidate for certification. Lin did not rehearse a triumphant meeting with the woman who had watched earlier work. She copied the reply deadline and turned to a more immediate task: making a safe place for the wet outer cloak without dripping on the letters she now wanted to keep legible.

lark_e03_after_019.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_019.text: The cloak peg sat beyond her comfortable reach. Lin asked the lodging keeper for a lower ordinary hook rather than using qi or testing an unassessed overhead movement to prove the room suited her. He supplied one from a repaired cupboard and asked whether its present height would work. She tried it with the dry cloak first. The change cost him a small amount of time and made her nightly habit easier. She thanked him for the actual work without treating it as a favor his whole household would now owe every future guest.

lark_e03_after_020.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_020.text: From the quieter lane window she could no longer see the freight gallery directly. She heard a bell and waited for the ordinary sequence to finish. No alarm called her onto a dark passage. Her accepted observation would take place with its actual people tomorrow. The four primary pairs in her record remained four, and the current comfortable body required food and rest as much as ambition. She laid out the first week's ordinary schedule, checked that its accepted hours did not overlap, and left the examination notebook closed.

lark_e03_after_021.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_021.text: In the room next door, a worker sang a song Lin recognized from a lower river market and changed the last line so it ended badly for the merchant. Somebody laughed and supplied a different ending in which the merchant married the mule. Lin did not know the original author or the pass's history of the joke. She listened until the singers grew bored and began discussing breakfast. A place could become familiar through details no formal application would ever ask her to demonstrate.

lark_e03_after_022.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_after_022.text: The first paid week had begun with work, meals and a room she could actually use. It also held unanswered questions about further instruction, the real gallery and the basket whose repair had brought Qin to her door. Lin would have to carry those questions alongside other people's irritation, kindness and habits. She did not need every person at the pass to approve the way she had arrived. She wanted enough continuing work to learn what they would find useful, and enough room to hear when the answer was not herself.

lark_e03_coda_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_coda_001.text: Before putting out the lamp, Lin found the lodging's winter notice beneath the meal list. Snow inspection could alter a posted passage before a scheduled shift. Workers would report to their keeper instead of crossing a closed line to preserve attendance. She copied the receiving point, not a promise of danger.

lark_e03_coda_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_coda_002.text: The notice also named a household cupboard for dry socks. Its keeper lent them under a return list, with no inspection of anyone's private papers. Lin checked that her own pair had dried and left the cupboard unused. Tomorrow's work would begin with ordinary feet inside shoes, which still mattered at fifth stage.

lark_e03_qin_result_gate.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_result_gate.text: Qin's dispatch terms paid four copper after a completed accepted load, or two for a stated canceled booking with its accepted waiting. They were his particular local terms, not a universal courier price. His two booked loads fell on Day Twenty-three; the replacement timing determined which could actually proceed. Lin waited while he read the result attached to her earlier choice.

lark_e03_qin_written_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_written_001.text: The timely written observation had reached the committee before its current replacement allocation closed. Qin had inspected and received the issued basket at the next morning collection. Its actual condition passed his keeper's ordinary check, and he completed both of the two accepted loads on their original dates. Their receivers signed the delivered scopes, after which his dispatcher paid four copper for each. The eight belonged to finished work, not to the fact that Lin had liked him enough to write a statement.

lark_e03_qin_written_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_written_002.text: He showed her the two receiving lines and asked whether she wanted to hear what the second household had put in the basket. Lin did. It had carried an enormous covered bean cake to a wedding whose cook had forgotten the bride disliked chestnuts. The cake arrived sound and the bride gave half away. Qin said people always imagined the dangerous part of freight ended when a basket reached its door. Lin laughed, then asked whether the recipient had agreed he could share that ordinary story. He said she had told him to tell it.

lark_e03_qin_written_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_written_003.text: The contractor had corrected its source book without blaming a witness for the old missing entry. Qin wanted the remaining replacement date recorded, since the issued one did not restore the damaged pair as a whole. Lin could hear an actual improvement and an unresolved work question in the same account. Her paper had helped him keep two paid opportunities. It had not bought his permanent confidence in every decision she might make at the pass. He took the receiving back before the employment meeting began.

lark_e03_qin_later_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_later_001.text: The accepted afternoon appearance had corrected the source after the first replacement allocation closed. Qin's first booked load was canceled under its waiting terms and paid two copper. The next stock arrival supplied a basket that he inspected and received before his second original booking. He completed that delivered scope and earned four after receiving. Six copper resulted from one canceled booking and one completed load. The first lost delivery had not been performed by someone insisting the later witness account was useful enough to erase its date.

lark_e03_qin_later_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_later_002.text: Qin had used the canceled interval to mend a small part of his ordinary equipment, but that work did not restore the missing load wage. The first recipient received the goods by a separately arranged route and no longer needed his original delivery. Lin asked whether he was angry with her. He said he had requested help and received the kind she had agreed to give. He also wished the source had reached the committee sooner. He could hold both judgments without instructing her which one their acquaintance must become.

lark_e03_qin_later_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_later_003.text: He showed her the corrected repair book and kept the actual dispatch payment beside it. Her later appearance had allowed the committee to ask direct questions, with one earlier opportunity already gone. Lin listened to the receiver's note without offering to purchase a warmer account of her choice. She would meet Qin again under work that might require trust. This conversation made its starting place clear enough that she could try to earn more of it through actual help rather than claiming the first favor had settled everything.

lark_e03_qin_referred_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_referred_001.text: The current keepers had eventually corrected the formal return from their own held records, without an additional statement from Lin. By that receiving date, both of Qin's original replacement-dependent load bookings had been canceled. Their accepted waiting terms paid two copper each, four in total. A later basket had now been inspected for new work, but it could not deliver two loads whose original dates and recipients had already moved on. The source had become accurate while the missed opportunities remained missed.

lark_e03_qin_referred_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_referred_002.text: Qin said he had nearly stopped asking Lin anything after the first refusal. Then Shan had reminded him that a newcomer could accept a finite application without becoming their household's unpaid advocate. He disliked how sensible that sounded when he had been the person waiting for a basket. Lin did not ask him to make the dislike disappear. She thanked him for telling her and said she would prefer an actual request she might accept to a friendly assumption she would eventually fail by not knowing it existed.

lark_e03_qin_referred_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e03_qin_referred_003.text: He kept the corrected book receiving and the two cancellation payments in his own account. Lin had preserved her preparation and afternoon, while he had relied on the current source process at a slower date. They could work near each other without pretending this result had made no difference. Qin left for his collecting route after asking the keeper to receive his present basket condition. Lin watched him go and understood that a relationship could remain possible without being restored to the ease it had had before someone needed help.
